title: CLAUDE.md
text: package uses centralized color palette system stored inst/extdata/: - benvi_colors.rds: Named color definitions (e.g., “AzulQuinto”, “Floresta”, “Violeta”) - benvi_palette.rds: Pre-built palette collections Palette Generation (data-raw/cols_to_palette.R): - Converts named colors hex values via get_colors() get_hex() functions - Creates palette sets organized type: - Theme palettes (4 colors): grays, browns, yellows, greens, blues, purples, pinks, oranges - Qualitative palettes (8 colors): qual_1 qual_9 - Sequential palettes (9 colors): seq_grays, seq_browns, seq_yellows, seq_greens, seq_blues, seq_purples, seq_pinks, seq_oranges - City-specific palettes: spo_seq, spo_div, spo_qual, rio_seq, rio_div, rio_qual, bhe_seq, bhe_div - Brand palettes: benvi_blue, benvi_purple, basic

title: CLAUDE.md
text: R/benvi_palette.R: - benvi_palette(pal_name, n, direction, type): Main palette accessor - Returns hex colors named palettes - Supports discrete (exact colors) continuous (interpolated) modes - Can reverse palettes direction = -1 - pal_pal(): Internal factory function creating palette generators - print.palette(): S3 method visualizing palettes R/palette_utils.R: - show_palettes(type, n): Visual display palettes (like RColorBrewer::display.brewer.()) R/benvi_scales.R: - Discrete scales: scale_color_benvi_d(), scale_fill_benvi_d() - Continuous scales: scale_color_benvi_c(), scale_fill_benvi_c() - use British/American spelling variants (color/colour) R/theme_benvi.R: - get_benvi_font_family(): Internal — checks Poppins installed, falls back “sans” - theme_custom(): Internal base theme - theme_benvi(): Exported custom ggplot2 theme Poppins font (falls back sans) R/fonts-modern.R (font management): - check_poppins_installed(): Internal — checks Poppins available via systemfonts (returns FALSE systemfonts installed) - install_poppins(): Downloads installs Poppins Google Fonts (requires systemfonts internet) - font_status(): Reports Poppins ragg availability recommendations R/save-plot.R: - ggsave_benvi(): Wrapper around ggplot2::ggsave() uses ragg device PNG available **R/plot_*.R** — wrapper functions (active): - plot_line(): Line chart - plot_column(): Column/bar chart (includes text labels, inside text via ggfittext) - plot_scatter(): Scatter plot optional regression line - plot_area(): Area chart - plot_histogram(): Histogram R/utils.R: - format_num_br(): Format numbers Brazilian locale (period thousands, comma decimal) R/utils-globals.R: Global variable bindings tidy eval (suppresses R CMD check notes) R/plot_scatter.R also exports: - plot_add_xy(): Helper add axis lines plot

title: Plot a histogram chart — plot_histogram
text: method parameter controls algorithm used compute optimal bin width. Available methods: "fd" "FD" Freedman-Diaconis rule (default). Robust outliers, uses IQR. Formula: \(2 * IQR / n^{1/3}\). Best distributions. "Scott" Scott's rule. Uses standard deviation. Formula: \(3 * sd / n^{1/3}\). Works well normal-like distributions. "Sturges" Sturges' formula. Simple logarithmic rule. Formula: \(k = \lceil log_2(n) \rceil\) bins. Good roughly normal data. "Rice" Rice rule. Cube root based. Formula: \(k = \lceil 2n^{1/3} \rceil\) bins. General purpose rule. "sqrt" Square root rule. Formula: \(k = \lceil \sqrt{n} \rceil\) bins. Simple, tends oversmooth. doubt, use default "fd" (Freedman-Diaconis), robust works well across different distributions.

title: Plot a histogram chart — plot_histogram
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ set.seed(5) tbl <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n = 1000))  # Default parameters use Freedman-Diaconis plot_histogram(data = tbl, x = x) # Use bins to manually choose number of bins plot_histogram(data = tbl, x = x, bins = 50) # Example of alternative methods: square root and Rice plot_histogram(data = tbl, x = x, method = "sqrt") plot_histogram(data = tbl, x = x, method = "Rice")  # To compare multiple groups use facet tbl <- data.frame( city = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each.out = 500), x = c(rnorm(500), runif(500), rexp(500)) ) plot_histogram(data = tbl, x = x, facet = city, density = TRUE) } # }
